name: The Deep Crawler
concept_focus: Hard Python: a real package with dataclasses, enums, generators, search algorithms, an installable CLI, events, decorators, context managers, logging, pytest, profiling and type checking

story.title: Below the Old Mine
story.client: Foreman Brigid of the collapsed Deepvein mine
story.hook: The Deepvein mine broke into the halls of Die Tozza van Zamalek, who rebuilds the maze every night and sells maps that lead nowhere. Brigid needs a crawler her miners can trust: a real package they can install, floors that are random but repeatable, a pathfinder that never lies, saves that survive a crash, and tests that prove all of it.

acts.title: Act I: The Gate
acts.goal: A real package and data you can trust: modules, dataclasses, enums, shared-state bugs and seeded floors.

acts.title: Act II: The Depths
acts.goal: Generators, breadth-first search, A*, fog of war, and a virtual environment with a crawl command.

acts.title: Act III: The Machinery
acts.goal: An event bus, decorators, context managers, an error family, closures and logging.

acts.title: Act IV: The Core
acts.goal: A pytest suite, profiling, type checking, A* from memory and a system of your own design.

boss_lore: Die Tozza van Zamalek runs the deep halls like a market: every corridor for sale, every map a little wrong, and the maze rebuilt every night. Nobody has reached the bottom with a working save.
boss_brief: Bring the finished deep_crawler package: installed with pip install -e . and run as crawl with --seed, --size and --radius; seeded floors with a guaranteed way down; BFS and A* that agree; fog of war; dataclass entities; an event bus, decorators and atomic saves through a context manager; logging; a passing pytest suite; mypy clean; and a README that explains install, run, test and the architecture.
boss_twist: The Tozza's halls shift: every five turns walls move. Write shift_walls(grid, rng) that toggles walls while keeping the stairs reachable (re-check with your pathfinder), make monsters re-plan their paths after a shift, and add tests proving the stairs stay reachable across 1,000 seeded shifts.

twist_2.label: Phase 2: The horde
twist_2.quest: The Tozza releases a horde: 200 monsters path toward the hero every turn. Profile a 100-turn run on a 60x60 floor, then make it finish in under two seconds (cache paths, reuse results, or compute one breadth-first distance map from the hero that every monster follows). Print the before and after timings.

twist_3.label: Phase 3: The corrupted save
twist_3.quest: The Tozza corrupts saves mid-write. Make saves versioned (a schema_version field and a migration from version 1 to version 2) and verified (a checksum), on top of atomic writes. Add tests: a crash halfway through a write never loses the last good save, a tampered save raises SaveCorrupted, and an old version 1 save still loads.

twist_4.label: Phase 4: Ship it
twist_4.quest: Release the crawler: build a wheel with python -m build, install it into a brand new virtual environment from the wheel, and run crawl --seed 7 there. Bump the version to 1.0.0, write CHANGELOG.md, and make sure the README's install steps work for someone who has never seen the project.

mobs.name: The Hollow Adventurer
mobs.concept: Packages, modules and a thin entry point
mobs.encounter: Make deep_crawler with a crawler package and a play.py launcher, and run it.
mobs.contract: Brigid's miners keep losing scripts in one giant file. Start the way real projects start: a folder, a package, and a thin door into it.

objectives.label: Shape the package
objectives.brief: Make the folder deep_crawler. Inside it create the package crawler/ (crawler/__init__.py with a __version__ = "0.1.0" line) and play.py, a launcher of three lines that imports crawler and prints its version. Run it from the terminal: cd deep_crawler, then python play.py.

objectives.label: Package or module
objectives.brief: Explain the difference between a module and a package, and what __init__.py does when you import crawler.

objectives.label: Predict the import
objectives.brief: Predict what happens if you run python play.py from the folder above deep_crawler instead of inside it, and why.

mobs.name: The Stat Golem
mobs.encounter: Model the hero and monsters as dataclasses with types, defaults and validation.
mobs.contract: The Golem is all numbers and no rules: health below zero, attack as a string. Give your creatures a shape that refuses nonsense.

objectives.label: Model the creatures
objectives.brief: In crawler/entities.py write @dataclass classes Hero and Monster with type hints: name, hp, max_hp, attack, defence and a position tuple, with sensible defaults.

objectives.label: Refuse nonsense
objectives.brief: Add __post_init__ validation so hp above max_hp, negative stats or a non-tuple position raise ValueError with a clear message.

objectives.label: Why dataclasses
objectives.brief: Explain what @dataclass writes for you (look at __init__, __repr__ and __eq__), and when you would still write a normal class.

mobs.name: The Enum Warden
mobs.encounter: Describe tiles and directions with Enums and act on them with match.
mobs.contract: The Warden speaks only in numbers: 0 is floor, 1 is wall, 7 is... nobody remembers. Give every tile and direction a real name.

objectives.label: Name the tiles
objectives.brief: In crawler/world.py define Tile (FLOOR, WALL, DOOR, STAIRS) and Direction (N, E, S, W with a (dx, dy) value) as Enums, and write describe(tile) using match with a case for every tile.

objectives.label: Enum or number
objectives.brief: Predict what Tile.WALL == 1 and Tile.WALL.value == 1 give, and explain why the first is safer to get wrong loudly.

mobs.name: The Shared Satchel
mobs.encounter: Find why every hero shares one inventory, and fix it.
mobs.contract: Two heroes walked in. One picked up a key, and both of them have it. Something in the satchel is shared.

objectives.label: Unshare the satchel
objectives.brief:
This is the rival crawler's hero:
```python
@dataclass
class Hero:
    name: str
    inventory: list = []
```
Run it and read the error, then explain why Python refuses it and why a normal class with def __init__(self, inventory=[]) is worse. Fix your Hero with field(default_factory=list).

objectives.label: Prove it
objectives.brief: Write a short script or test showing two heroes picking up different items and keeping separate inventories.

objectives.label: Names and objects
objectives.brief: Explain the difference between two names pointing at one list and two separate lists, using id() or is.

mobs.name: The Seeded Maze
mobs.encounter: Generate a dungeon floor from a seed, with a path guaranteed from start to stairs.
mobs.contract: Every miner wants a fresh floor, and Brigid wants to replay the one that killed them. Make floors random and repeatable.

objectives.label: Carve the floor
objectives.brief: Write generate_floor(width, height, seed) in crawler/world.py that returns a grid of Tiles using its own random.Random(seed), never the global random.

objectives.label: Guarantee a way down
objectives.brief: Flood-fill from the start; if the stairs are unreachable, carve a corridor or regenerate, so every floor can be finished.

objectives.label: Same seed, same floor
objectives.brief: Add tests that the same seed gives the same floor, different seeds usually differ, and the stairs are always reachable over 200 seeds.

objectives.label: Why its own Random
objectives.brief: Explain why a private random.Random(seed) beats calling random.seed() at the top of the program.

mobs.name: The Wandering Eye
mobs.encounter: Yield the moves a creature can make instead of building lists.
mobs.contract: The Eye looks everywhere at once and drowns in it. Teach it to look one step at a time.

objectives.label: Yield the moves
objectives.brief: Write neighbours(grid, pos) as a generator that yields each walkable (x, y) next to pos, using your Direction enum.

objectives.label: Predict laziness
objectives.brief: Predict what printing neighbours(grid, (1, 1)) shows before and after wrapping it in list(), and what happens if you loop over the same generator twice.

objectives.label: Why yield
objectives.brief: Explain when a generator beats returning a list, in memory and in time.

mobs.name: The Pathfinder
mobs.encounter: Find the shortest path across the floor, or report there is none.
mobs.contract: Miners keep dying in dead ends. The Pathfinder knows the shortest way and will not tell you; work it out yourself.

objectives.label: Breadth-first
objectives.brief: Write shortest_path(grid, start, goal) in crawler/pathfinding.py with breadth-first search and collections.deque, returning the list of positions, or None when there is no way.

objectives.label: Test the edges
objectives.brief: Test a straight corridor, a maze with one route, start == goal, and an unreachable goal.

objectives.label: Why shortest
objectives.brief: Explain why breadth-first search finds the shortest path on a grid where every step costs the same.

mobs.name: The Star Seeker
mobs.encounter: Find paths faster with A*, a priority queue and a heuristic.
mobs.contract: On a big floor your breadth-first search crawls. The Seeker moves toward the goal on purpose. Learn its trick.

objectives.label: Write A*
objectives.brief: Write astar(grid, start, goal) in crawler/pathfinding.py using heapq and a Manhattan-distance heuristic, returning the same paths as your BFS.

objectives.label: Count the work
objectives.brief: Count the nodes each search expands and print both counts on a 60x60 floor.

objectives.label: Same answers
objectives.brief: Add parametrised tests that astar and shortest_path return paths of equal length on 50 seeded floors.

objectives.label: The heuristic's rule
objectives.brief: Explain why Manhattan distance never overestimates on this grid, and what goes wrong if a heuristic does.

mobs.name: The Fog Weaver
mobs.encounter: Track what the hero sees now and what they have explored, with sets.
mobs.contract: The Weaver hides the floor. Remember what you have seen, and show only what you can see.

objectives.label: What you see
objectives.brief: Write visible_from(grid, pos, radius) returning a set of positions within radius that are not behind a wall in a straight line.

objectives.label: What you remember
objectives.brief: Keep an explored set that grows with each move, and draw unexplored tiles as fog, seen tiles normally and remembered tiles dimmed.

objectives.label: Set algebra
objectives.brief: Predict the result of visible - explored, visible & explored and explored | visible after two moves, then check.

mobs.name: The Venv Smith
mobs.concept: Virtual environments, pyproject and a CLI
mobs.encounter: Install your crawler into a virtual environment and give it a real command.
mobs.contract: Brigid's miners each have different Python setups, and nothing works twice. Give the crawler a home of its own and a command anyone can type.

objectives.label: Make a home
objectives.brief: Create a virtual environment in deep_crawler (python -m venv .venv), activate it, and add .venv to a .gitignore. Show which python is active in the terminal.

objectives.label: Describe the project
objectives.brief: Write pyproject.toml with the project's name, version, Python requirement and a console script crawl = "crawler.cli:main", then pip install -e . inside the environment.

objectives.label: A real command
objectives.brief: Write crawler/cli.py with argparse: crawl --seed 42 --size 30 --radius 4, with help text, validation and sensible defaults, and run it as crawl from the terminal.

objectives.label: Why a virtual environment
objectives.brief: Explain what a virtual environment isolates, and what pip install -e . does differently from pip install .

mobs.name: The Event Herald
mobs.encounter: Let parts of the game react to events without knowing about each other.
mobs.contract: Every system shouts at every other system. The Herald proposes a better way: announce events, and let whoever cares listen.

objectives.label: Build the bus
objectives.brief: Write crawler/events.py with an EventBus that has subscribe(name, handler) and emit(name, **data), and use it so a monster's death fires monster_died.

objectives.label: Predict the order
objectives.brief: Predict the order handlers run in when three subscribe to the same event, and what happens if one raises.

objectives.label: Why events
objectives.brief: Explain how the event bus lets you add a scoreboard without editing the combat code.

mobs.name: The Decorator Monk
mobs.encounter: Wrap actions with logging and cooldowns using your own decorators.
mobs.contract: The Monk adds rules to actions without touching them. Learn to wrap a function in another one.

objectives.label: Log every action
objectives.brief: Write a @log_action decorator that records the action's name and arguments each time it runs, and use functools.wraps so the name survives.

objectives.label: Cooldowns
objectives.brief: Write @cooldown(turns) so a decorated ability raises AbilityOnCooldown if used again too soon, and test it.

objectives.label: Why wraps
objectives.brief: Explain what breaks (help(), __name__, tracebacks) when a decorator forgets functools.wraps.

mobs.name: The Context Keeper
mobs.encounter: Save safely with a context manager and give errors their own family.
mobs.contract: Saves vanish when the crawler crashes mid-write. The Keeper only trusts code that cleans up after itself.

objectives.label: An error family
objectives.brief: Define CrawlerError and subclasses (SaveCorrupted, AbilityOnCooldown, InvalidMove) in crawler/errors.py, and raise them instead of bare Exception.

objectives.label: Save atomically
objectives.brief: Write a context manager atomic_write(path) with contextlib that writes to a temporary file and only replaces the real save when the block finishes without an error.

objectives.label: Save and load
objectives.brief: Save and load the hero, floor seed and explored set as JSON through atomic_write, and turn a broken file into SaveCorrupted.

objectives.label: What with does
objectives.brief: Explain what __enter__ and __exit__ do, and why the temporary file must be cleaned up even when an exception escapes.

mobs.name: The Silent Saboteur
mobs.encounter: Find why every button runs the last action.
mobs.contract: The Saboteur rewired the hotkeys. Press 1, 2 or 3 and you always cast the last spell.

objectives.label: Rewire the hotkeys
objectives.brief:
The rival crawler binds hotkeys like this:
```python
hotkeys = {}
for number, spell in enumerate(['fire', 'ice', 'storm'], 1):
    hotkeys[number] = lambda: cast(spell)
```
Every key casts storm. Explain late binding in a comment and fix it two ways: a default argument and functools.partial.

objectives.label: Pin it with a test
objectives.brief: Write a test that fails on the broken version and passes on yours.

objectives.label: Closures
objectives.brief: Explain what a closure captures: the value, or the variable?

mobs.name: The Lantern Keeper
mobs.encounter: Replace prints with logging and debug a failing run from its log.
mobs.contract: Down here, print statements vanish into the dark. The Keeper reads logs, levels and timestamps.

objectives.label: Light the lanterns
objectives.brief: Configure logging once in crawler/cli.py: INFO to the terminal, DEBUG to deep_crawler.log with timestamps, and use logging.getLogger(__name__) in every module.

objectives.label: Retire print
objectives.brief: Replace debugging prints across the package with log calls at the right level (debug, info, warning, error).

objectives.label: Debug from the log
objectives.brief: Break a floor on purpose (no stairs), run it, and find the cause using only deep_crawler.log; paste the log lines that gave it away in a comment.

objectives.label: Choose a level
objectives.brief: Explain when you would use debug, info, warning and error, and why the log file and the terminal show different levels.

mobs.name: The Test Legion
mobs.encounter: Grow the tests into a suite with fixtures, parametrize and tmp_path.
mobs.contract: The Legion marches in formation: every test sets up the same way. Stop copying setup code into every test.

objectives.label: Shared fixtures
objectives.brief: Create tests/conftest.py with fixtures for a small seeded floor, a hero and an event bus, and use them across your tests.

objectives.label: Test the saves
objectives.brief: Test save and load with tmp_path, including a corrupted file raising SaveCorrupted.

objectives.label: Read the run
objectives.brief: Run pytest -q from deep_crawler. Explain what the dots, F and E mean, and how pytest -k and -x help you.

mobs.name: The Profiler
mobs.encounter: Profile the search on a huge floor and make it faster.
mobs.contract: On a 200x200 floor your crawler freezes. Guessing is forbidden; measure first.

objectives.label: Measure
objectives.brief: Profile astar on a 200x200 floor with cProfile and timeit, and write the slowest functions and timings in a comment.

objectives.label: Make it fast
objectives.brief: Fix the hotspot (for example a list used as the closed set, or recomputed neighbours) and show the speed-up with the same measurement.

objectives.label: Why it was slow
objectives.brief: Explain in Big-O terms why checking membership in a list is slow and in a set is fast.

mobs.name: The Type Inquisitor
mobs.encounter: Type the whole package and make mypy happy.
mobs.contract: The Inquisitor trusts no argument it cannot name. Type everything and let a checker prove it.

objectives.label: Type the package
objectives.brief: Add type hints to every public function in the package, including return types and Optional where something can be None.

objectives.label: Pass mypy
objectives.brief: pip install mypy in your environment, run mypy crawler, and fix every error it reports; paste the clean result in a comment.

objectives.label: A Protocol
objectives.brief: Define a Mover Protocol (position plus move()) in crawler/entities.py and type pathfinding helpers against it, so Hero and Monster both fit without inheritance.

objectives.label: Why types
objectives.brief: Explain what mypy can catch before you run anything, and what it can never catch.

mobs.name: The Amnesiac
mobs.encounter: Rebuild A* from memory in a blank file and prove it.
mobs.contract: The Amnesiac forgets every route the moment it walks it. Prove you will not.

objectives.label: Rebuild it
objectives.brief: Close crawler/pathfinding.py. In a new file memory_astar.py, write A* on a grid from memory, with heapq and a Manhattan heuristic.

objectives.label: Check it
objectives.brief: Under it, compare your rebuild with crawler.pathfinding.astar on 20 seeded floors and assert equal path lengths.

objectives.label: Compare
objectives.brief: What did you remember straight away, and what did you have to reason out again?

mobs.name: The Architect
mobs.encounter: Design and build a new system for the crawler, wired through events.
mobs.contract: Brigid's last request: something nobody asked for. Design a system of your own and build it the way the rest of the crawler is built.

objectives.label: Design it first
objectives.brief: Write a design section in README.md: what your system does (traps, crafting, a merchant, monster factions...), the dataclasses it needs and the events it listens to.

objectives.label: Build it
objectives.brief: Build it in its own module, wired through the event bus, with tests for its rules.

objectives.label: Defend it
objectives.brief: Explain one trade-off you made and what you would change with another week.
